name: l01_long_narration
description: Long narration (~616 words, about 4-5 minutes of speech)

request.script: Here is a simple way to build a monthly budget. First, write down your take-home pay. Next, list your fixed costs like rent, electricity and your phone bill. Then track what you spend on food and transport for one week. Put a fixed amount into savings on payday, before you spend anything else. Review your notes every Sunday evening and adjust. In three months you will know exactly where your money goes. City officials announced on Monday that two hundred electric buses will join the public fleet by next year. The buses will charge overnight at three new depots on the edge of the city. Officials say the change should cut diesel use and make streets quieter. Commuters will see the first buses on the busiest routes in the spring. Fares will stay the same. Meet PlanPlate, the app that plans your meals for the week. Tell it what you like, and it builds a shopping list in seconds. Cook fresh vegetables, save money, and waste less food. Your family gets healthy dinners without the daily stress. Download it today and get your evenings back. Every morning, an old gardener walked to the edge of the village with a small watering can. He had planted a single seed in a quiet corner of the field. For weeks nothing happened, and the neighbours laughed. But he kept watering the soil, day after day. One spring morning, a tiny green shoot pushed through the earth. Years later, children played in the shade of a tall tree. Patience, he said, is how great things grow. Cloud computing means your files and programs live on servers in large data centers, not on your own laptop. A small team can rent that computing power by the hour. Developers often write Python scripts to automate the boring parts of their work. With a few clicks of a mouse, a new server can be running in minutes. This flexibility has changed how startups grow. Saving money is not about earning more. It is about small habits that you repeat every day. Start by keeping coins in a glass jar on your desk. Cook at home a few nights a week instead of ordering food. Before you buy something, wait one day and ask if you really need it. Compare prices at different shops, and use a shopping list. Put a fixed amount into a savings account the moment your salary arrives. Watch the balance grow slowly, month after month. Value is not only money; it is the security and freedom that savings give your family. Trust the process, because wealth is earned slowly. Trust is earned slowly. Sales grew forty percent in 2025, driven by small shops that moved online. Three out of four customers now pay with their phones. Growth like this does not happen by luck. It comes from teams that listen, plan, and keep improving every single week. Rooftop solar panels turn sunlight into electricity. Each panel is made of many small cells. When light hits a cell, it creates a flow of electric current. An inverter changes that current into the kind of power your home uses. On sunny days, extra energy can flow back to the grid. A typical panel lasts more than twenty years with very little maintenance. Before sunrise, the city is quiet. Delivery vans move through empty streets. The first trains roll across the bridge. Cafes switch on their lights and the smell of coffee fills the air. By eight o'clock, the roads are full of traffic and the skyline glows in the morning sun. From the farm field to your kitchen table in one day. Fresh vegetables, picked this morning and delivered by noon.
